analysis.title: GS Blekos - Marketcolour + Flows / Eni / Sika / Norsk Hydro / Siemens Energy 26 Oct 2026
key_insights: US equities fell on the week: SPX -52bps to 7623, NDX unchanged at 28957, RTY -29bps to 2775. 8 of 11 sectors fell (Consumer Staples -1.83%, Energy +2.51%, Tech +0.35%).
Signs of stabilization in the AI trade on Friday: the GS AI Semis basket (GSCBSMHX) rose 0.86%, while the neocloud Data Center basket (GSXUNEOC) fell 0.77%.
In Europe, EU Big Oils (GSXEBOIE) rose 4.6% and were the dominant outperformer. UK Homebuilders (GSSBUKHO) rose 1.2% as gilt yields stabilised. Luxury (GSXELUXG) fell 4.8% and was the worst basket.

SPX 60-day realized volatility is about 10%, in the bottom quartile of the COVID and post-COVID era. The GS Momentum basket is up more than 5% in the period, more than in 2000, 2009 or 2020, with 2 months left in the year.

GS trading floor saw about $20bn of net TMT (Info Tech + Comm Services) selling over the past 2 weeks across all client types and execution channels. This approaches the -$23bn net sold over 2 weeks in the July AI selling episode.

Hedge funds net sold US equities for a 3rd straight week (4 of the last 5), driven by long and short sales in single stocks. This was the largest de-grossing since late July. Industrials were among the most net sold sectors, with HFs selling the group at the fastest pace in 6+ months.
Real Estate and Staples were the most net bought US sectors, which points to a defensive posture.
US L/S gross leverage rose 2.2 pts to 216.1% (64th percentile one-year). Net leverage fell 0.3 pts to 43.4% (0th percentile five-year).
Fundamental L/S managers lost 1.1% on the week (alpha -0.3%) and are down 3.8% MTD. That gives back a quarter of 2026 performance. They are still up 8.8% YTD, from +17.4% at end of June.

CTAs are long $38.5bn of S&P futures (91st percentile), nearly 80% of aggregate net longs across the 21 markets tracked. The S&P is already below its short-term trend threshold, and the more important medium-term level is about 1.3% below Friday's close.

This week has FOMC and BOC on Wednesday, ECB on Thursday and BOJ on Friday, plus the heaviest week of Q3 earnings (44% of S&P market cap reports). MSFT, GOOG, NOW and KLAC report Wednesday. AMZN and INTC report Thursday.

GS forecasts one more ECB hike in December. A March hike is possible if energy prices keep rising, especially gas in a cold winter. GS sees a significant hurdle to faster hikes or a deposit rate above 3%.
Norsk Hydro is cut to Neutral with a NOK 79 price target, down from NOK 100. EBITDA estimates for 2026/27 fall 6%/6% on lower Aluminium, Metal Markets and Energy earnings and higher gas costs.
ENI is Buy with a EUR29 price target. EPS estimates rise 6.7%/11.0%/12.5% for 2026E/27E/28E on a lower tax rate and a higher dividend.
Sika is Conviction List Buy with a CHF225 target. GS sees upside from easing raw material and energy costs, with 2028 EBITDA 4% above consensus.
Siemens Energy is Conviction List Buy with a EUR212 target. The Capital Markets Day on Nov 11 is the next step in the re-rating story. GS forecasts group EBITA up about 6x between FY2025 and FY2030.
HFs net sold global Energy at the fastest pace in over 5 months. Global Staples was the most net bought sector in dollar terms, at the fastest pace in 10 weeks.

market_movers.rationale: 2026/27 EBITDA cut 6% on lower Aluminium, Metal Markets and Energy earnings and higher gas costs. Target now rests on a 50/50 blend of 1x NAV and 5.5x EV/EBITDA, down from 6.5x. About 10% upside.

EPS estimates rise 6.7%/11.0%/12.5% for 2026E/27E/28E on a lower tax rate and higher dividend. Trades at about a 20% premium to EU Big Oils on 5.6x 2026E EV/DACF, which GS calls justified. About 10% upside.

On the Conviction List. 2028 EBITDA is 4% above consensus, rising to 7% if raw material costs revert to 2025 levels. Trades on about 23x P/E, a 20% discount to its historical average. About 25% upside.
On the Conviction List. GS forecasts group EBITA up about 6x between FY2025 and FY2030, 11% above Bloomberg consensus by FY2030. Shares trade on about 5x 2030E EV/EBITDA. About 80% upside.

sector_views.rationale: EU Big Oils outperformed by 4.6% and US Energy rose 2.51% on the week, while HFs net sold global Energy at the fastest pace in over 5 months.
US Staples fell 1.83% on the week, while HFs net bought Staples at the fastest pace in 10 weeks as part of a defensive posture.

earnings_insights: Q3 earnings season is at its heaviest this week, with 44% of S&P market cap reporting. MSFT, GOOG, NOW and KLAC report Wednesday. AMZN and INTC report Thursday.
ENI estimate changes: EPS +6.7%/+11.0%/+12.5% for 2026E/27E/28E (GS estimates, not reported figures), driven by a lower tax rate and higher dividend. Trades on 5.6x 2026E EV/DACF.
Norsk Hydro GS estimate changes: 2026/27 EBITDA -6%/-6%, 2028 EBITDA +4% on cost revisions (GS estimates).
Sika GS 2028 EBITDA is 4% above consensus, and 7% above if raw material costs revert to 2025 levels (GS estimate vs consensus). Stock trades on about 23x P/E.
Siemens Energy GS forecasts FY2030 group EBITA 11% above Bloomberg consensus (GS estimate), with shares on about 5x 2030E EV/EBITDA.
